orders.reason: headaches and poor concentration after a major work stressor

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Headaches, poor focus
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Last appt of the day. About 6 wks of a dull, all-over headache most days, builds through the afternoon, worst by evening. No nausea or vomiting, no light or sound sensitivity, no waking from sleep, no worst-ever headache, no neuro symptoms. Also can't concentrate, rereads emails.
Started right after his company announced layoffs and a restructuring. He's been running the restructuring plan for his division, 12-hr days, says he hasn't had time to think about what it means for him. Sleep 5-6 hrs. Alcohol unchanged.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25.

Exam: BP 141/96, HR 70. Tense but appropriate. Neck supple, mild trapezius tightness. Cranial nerves intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal. Fundi: discs flat as far as I can see.
PHQ-9 9, GAD-7 8.

A/P
1. Daily headache with poor concentration in the setting of a big work stressor; nonfocal exam. CBC, CMP, TSH to be thorough. Referral to psychiatry for evaluation and therapy options - he's open to it.
2. HTN a bit high today, likely stress; continue meds.
3. RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Referral to psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral: Psychiatry / Behavioral Health. 47M with ADPKD and HTN, six weeks of daily headaches and poor concentration that began with layoff news at work. Nonfocal neuro exam. PHQ-9 9, GAD-7 8, no SI. CBC, CMP, TSH pending. Requesting evaluation and therapy options.

documents.title: Blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn, blood counts, metabolic panel (including kidney function) and thyroid are all normal. Psychiatry should call this week; let me know if they don't.

documents.title: Psychiatric evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Behavioral Health - Initial Psychiatric Evaluation
Date of service: 03/15/2022

Reason for referral: two months of headaches and poor concentration.

History: 47-year-old married man with ADPKD and hypertension. Daily, dull, diffuse headaches that worsen toward evening; denies nausea, vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia. Difficulty concentrating at work. Onset closely followed the announcement of layoffs at the company where he has worked for 15 years. Since then he has thrown himself into preparing his division for the restructuring and admits he has not stopped to consider what it means for him personally. No prior psychiatric history, no suicidal thoughts, no substance use beyond social alcohol.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (lisinopril per patient). NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78. Neurological screen without focal findings; remainder unremarkable.
Labs reviewed: CBC, CMP and TSH normal (02/2022).

Mental status: well groomed, cooperative, mildly anxious affect, linear thought process, no psychosis, insight fair.

Diagnosis: adjustment disorder, in response to an occupational stressor.

Plan: weekly individual psychotherapy (CBT-based) with one of our therapists for about 8-10 sessions, focusing on stress and sleep. No medication indicated at this time. Re-evaluate in 2 months.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Follow-up 05/24/2022. Has attended 8 therapy sessions. Headaches now a couple of times a week and milder; concentration improved; sleeping closer to 7 hours. Mood euthymic. Adjustment disorder improving. Will finish the therapy block and follow up with us as needed. No medications from this office.

documents.title: Cancelled physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, cancelling tomorrow's 8am physical, work crunch. Will call back to rebook after the end of the quarter.

documents.title: Refill: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 90-day supply approved. No BP visit since 9/2020 other than 2/2022 headache visit, no BMP since February. Please have him schedule a BP visit with labs before next refill.

documents.title: Time for a visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Glenn, your refills went to the pharmacy. The doctor would like to see you for a blood pressure check and blood work before the next ones. You can book online or reply here.

documents.title: We missed you today
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: We missed you at 12:20 today. Please reply or call to reschedule your blood pressure visit.

documents.title: Bridge refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 30-day bridge of lisinopril and HCTZ only. Missed 12/13 visit. Front desk to call and book.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 74. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T wave abnormality.

orders.reason: exertional dyspnea, wide pulse pressure, murmur

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit in about a year; missed his BP follow-ups through the restructuring. Comes in because over the past few months he's been more winded - stairs at work, carrying groceries - and can't keep up on the weekend walks. Also notices his heart pounding in his chest when he lies on his left side at night. No chest pain, no fainting, no leg swelling, no orthopnea.
Stress better; finished therapy last spring, headaches mostly gone.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 - admits some missed doses.

Exam: BP 149/52 (repeated, similar), HR 76 regular. SpO2 normal. Bounding radial pulses. Diastolic murmur along the left sternal border, heard best sitting forward. Lungs clear. No JVD, no edema.
ECG: sinus, normal.

A/P
1. Exertional dyspnea with a wide pulse pressure and a diastolic murmur: concern for aortic valve leak. Referred to cardiology, asked for a prompt appointment; they'll do the echo.
2. HTN, systolic high. Take the meds every day; we'll adjust once cardiology weighs in.
3. Adjustment disorder - resolved.
4. Overdue labs/physical: will do after cardiology.
RTC after cardiology.

documents.title: Referral to cardiology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral: Cardiology, please see within 2-3 weeks. 48M with HTN and ADPKD. Months of exertional dyspnea, pounding heartbeat lying on the left side. BP 149/52, bounding pulses, diastolic murmur at LSB. ECG sinus, normal. Question aortic regurgitation; echo requested. Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

events.reason: progressive shortness of breath, reduced exercise tolerance

reports.text: Left ventricle mildly dilated with normal wall thickness. LVEF 55% by biplane method, no regional wall motion abnormality. Normal diastolic filling for age. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation; no aortic stenosis. Mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant abnormality. Ascending aorta aneurysmally dilated; aortic root normal. No pericardial effusion. Estimated RV systolic pressure normal.
reports.conclusion: Moderate aortic regurgitation. Aneurysm of the ascending aorta. Mildly dilated left ventricle with LVEF 55%.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Lungs are clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. No pulmonary edema. Bones unremarkable.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - Consultation
Date of visit: 03/27/2023

Reason: worsening breathlessness and exercise intolerance.

HPI: 48-year-old man with ADPKD and hypertension, followed by nephrology and primary care, with a few months of progressive dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance and a pounding sensation in the chest, most noticeable lying on his left side. By his account his blood pressure has not been looked after for about a year and he has missed doses; it has been poorly controlled.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father ADPKD with ESRD at 62; paternal grandfather died at 58 of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm; mother hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Social: never smoker, 2-3 drinks/week, senior operations manager.

Exam: BP 150/50. Bounding peripheral pulses with a brisk carotid upstroke; nail-bed pulsations visible with light pressure on the nail tip. Diastolic murmur at the left sternal border. No peripheral edema. Lungs clear.

Studies today:
- Echo: moderate aortic regurgitation, trileaflet valve; aneurysm of the ascending aorta; LV mildly dilated, EF 55%.
- CXR: enlarged cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields.

Assessment:
1. Aortic regurgitation, moderate, with preserved LV function.
2. Ascending aortic aneurysm - needs exact sizing.
3. Hypertension, poorly controlled.

Plan: CT angiography of the chest to measure the aorta; I will see him back after it. Strict BP control and daily adherence; we discussed avoiding heavy straining/lifting. Will send recommendations to primary care.

reports.text:
CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, ECG-gated.
Aortic root at the sinuses normal. The ascending aorta measures 4.5 cm in maximal diameter, measured perpendicular to the vessel centerline at the level of the right pulmonary artery. No dissection flap, no intramural hematoma. Aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta normal in caliber. Pulmonary arteries normal. Heart enlarged; no pericardial effusion. Lungs clear. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen: partially imaged upper poles of both kidneys contain cysts, consistent with known polycystic kidney disease.
reports.conclusion: Ascending aortic aneurysm, 4.5 cm. No dissection. Arch and descending aorta normal caliber.

documents.title: CT angiogram reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT angiography reviewed: ascending aorta 4.5 cm, no dissection. Cardiology to follow up. BP control is key - he has a visit with us next month.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology follow-up 05/03/2023.
CT angiography: ascending aorta 4.5 cm without dissection; arch and descending aorta normal.
Symptoms unchanged, mild. Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 (reports taking daily now).
Impression: moderate aortic regurgitation with preserved EF; 4.5 cm ascending aortic aneurysm, below a surgical threshold.
Plan: surveillance echo and aortic imaging in 12 months, sooner for symptoms. Blood pressure control is the main lever; we would appreciate primary care's help getting him under 130/80. Return in a year.

documents.title: Cardiology letter
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, called pt to set up a BP visit after cardiology's letter. Booked 5/23 4:15 pm. Reminded to bring home cuff.

events.reason: shortness of breath and fatigue, palpitations

reports.text: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 130/min. Sawtooth flutter waves in II, III and aVF at about 260/min with 2:1 atrioventricular conduction. Normal axis. No acute ST elevation.

Limited study during tachycardia. Left ventricle dilated with global hypokinesis; LVEF 35% by visual estimate. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Aortic valve trileaflet; regurgitation not well assessed at this heart rate. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department Physician Record - received by fax
Date of visit: 09/16/2023

CC: shortness of breath, fatigue.

HPI: 49M with ADPKD and HTN, seen by cardiology 6 months ago for dyspnea, presents with worsening. Palpitations for months: fast and regular, several times weekly, at times lasting hours. Dyspnea and fatigue progressively worse over half a year. Denies chest pain, syncope, leg swelling. Ran out of his blood pressure pills several weeks ago and has not been taking them.

PMH: ADPKD, HTN, aortic regurgitation, ascending aortic aneurysm, psychogenic ED, adjustment disorder.
Home meds (listed): lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily - not taking.
Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: BP 150/95, HR 130, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: alert, comfortable at rest. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular and fast; no murmur, rub or gallop appreciated. No edema.

Results: Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0. BNP 80. TSH 2.5. Troponin not elevated. CBC unremarkable.
ECG: atrial flutter with 2:1 block, rate 130.
Bedside/formal echo: dilated LV, EF 35%.

ED course: IV metoprolol with rate to the 90s. Duration of flutter unknown (likely months); anticoagulation started. Cardiology consulted.

Impression: atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response; new LV dysfunction, likely tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Disposition: placed in cardiology observation.

events.reason: atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response, reduced ejection fraction

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Observation discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology Observation Unit - Discharge Summary
Admitted 09/16/2023, discharged 09/17/2023.

Diagnoses: atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response; LV systolic dysfunction (EF 35%), suspected tachycardia-mediated; hypertension (off medications at presentation); moderate aortic regurgitation; ascending aortic aneurysm 4.5 cm; ADPKD.

Course: rate controlled overnight on metoprolol, heart rate 80s-90s, remained in flutter. No heart failure signs. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (hypertension, LV dysfunction); apixaban started. Plan for cavotricuspid isthmus ablation after at least 3 weeks of uninterrupted anticoagulation.

Discharge medications:
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (new)
- apixaban 5 mg twice daily (new)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (resume)
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (resume)

Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks; electrophysiology will call to schedule ablation. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED and observation records came in this morning. Called Glenn. Feels better, heart not racing. Has the metoprolol and apixaban, filled both. Back on lisinopril and HCTZ - says he let them run out in the summer and didn't call. Not judging, but he needs to take all four every day; apixaban especially can't be skipped before the ablation. Visit next Tuesday.

events.reason: follow-up after ED visit for atrial flutter

documents.title: Post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 10 days after ED/obs stay for atrial flutter 2:1, EF 35% on echo, felt to be rate-related cardiomyopathy.
Since discharge: less winded, no palpitations he can feel, no bleeding on apixaban, no dizziness. Taking metoprolol succinate 50, apixaban 5 bid, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 - using a pill organizer now.

Exam: BP 132/70, HR 84 regular. Lungs clear. Diastolic murmur LSB. No JVD, no edema.

A/P
1. Atrial flutter, rate controlled. Apixaban uninterrupted ahead of ablation (EP scheduling). Med rec done.
2. LV dysfunction, likely tachycardia-mediated - expect improvement once rhythm controlled; cardiology to repeat echo.
3. HTN with AR/ascending aneurysm - much better back on meds. BMP today.
4. ADPKD - creatinine 1.0 in ED.
Call with any bleeding, fainting or racing heart.

documents.title: Medication list
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your medicines now: metoprolol succinate 50 mg once daily; apixaban 5 mg twice daily - do not miss doses, especially before your ablation; lisinopril 20 mg once daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily. Call us for bleeding, black stools, fainting or a racing heartbeat. Lab today for potassium and kidney function.

events.reason: cavotricuspid isthmus ablation for atrial flutter

documents.title: Electrophysiology procedure report
documents.author: cardiac electrophysiology
documents.body:
Electrophysiology Laboratory - Procedure Report
Date: 10/24/2023
Procedure: electrophysiology study and radiofrequency ablation of the cavotricuspid isthmus.
Indication: typical atrial flutter with tachycardia-mediated LV dysfunction; on apixaban uninterrupted for over 4 weeks.
Access: right femoral vein, ultrasound guided.
Findings: patient in atrial flutter on arrival, cycle length consistent with typical counterclockwise flutter, confirmed isthmus-dependent by entrainment. Linear ablation across the isthmus terminated flutter to sinus rhythm; bidirectional block confirmed. No other arrhythmia inducible.
Complications: none. Hemostasis with a figure-of-eight stitch.
Plan: continue apixaban for at least 3 months, continue metoprolol, repeat echocardiogram in about 3 months. Same-day discharge.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu L deltoid, updated COVID R deltoid. On apixaban - held pressure 2 min each site, no bleeding. Says ablation went fine last week, groin site healed.
